{{short description|American biologist}}
'''Jack Dixon''' is the Distinguished Professor of [[Pharmacology]], [[Cell biology|Cellular]] & [[Molecular medicine|Molecular Medicine]], [[Chemistry]] & [[Biochemistry]] at the [[UC San Diego School of Medicine|University of California San Diego School of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jack Dixon Faculty Bio - Dept. of Cellular & Molecular Medicine - UC San Diego|url=https://medschool.ucsd.edu:443/som/cmm/faculty/Pages/Jack-Dixon.aspx|access-date=2020-06-10|website=UC San Diego School of Medicine|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Dixon was born in 1943. He attended the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], where he earned a PhD in 1971.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Jack Dixon to Retire as HHMI Vice President and Chief Scientific Officer|url=https://www.hhmi.org/news/jack-dixon-retire-hhmi-vice-president-and-chief-scientific-officer|access-date=2020-06-10|website=HHMI.org|language=en}}</ref> He also studied at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UC Los Angeles]] and [[University of California, San Diego|UC San Diego]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Jack Dixon|url=https://iem.ucsd.edu/people/profiles/jack_dixon.html|access-date=2020-06-10|website=iem.ucsd.edu|archive-date=2020-06-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200610090208/https://iem.ucsd.edu/people/profiles/jack_dixon.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dixon joined the faculty of [[Purdue University]] in 1973 where he became the Wiley Professor of Biochemistry. He then worked at the [[University of Michigan]], where he became the chairman of the department of biological chemistry and was the [[Minor J. Coon]] Professor of Biological Chemistry. In 2003 Dixon went to UC San Diego, where he became dean for scientific affairs and professor in the department of pharmacology. Three years later he accepted the position of vice president and chief scientific officer at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]], and served there from 2007 until 2013.<ref name=":0" /> In July 2013 he went back to laboratory work and university work full time at UCSD.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards and honors ==
Dixon was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2000, in Biochemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jack Dixon|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/jack-e-dixon-9jpemv/|access-date=2020-06-10|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> He received the William Rose and Merck Awards ([[American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]]); was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]] and is a Foreign Member of the [[Royal Society]].<ref name=":1" /> He is also a member of the [[National Academy of Medicine|Institute of Medicine]].<ref name=":0" />
